description:
Returns dated signals for the companies in one watchlist, grouped by company. Reading
never scans; to bring a list up to date, that is scan_watchlist.

Pass since_last_pull to get only what has been recorded since the last complete pull
of this list, which includes older events a recent scan only just found. Otherwise it
covers the last `days`, or everything from `since`, by the date of the event.

Each company carries `total_signals`, how many it has in the window after the same
filters and the number to report, and `signal_count`, how many this response carries
(at most signals_per_company).

Companies with nothing in the window are listed separately with their scan state.
Where signal_absence_is_meaningful is false, that company is unconfirmed, not quiet.

Pages run over companies. Follow next_cursor to reach the whole list, because a pull
only counts as complete at the last page.

Cost: 12 credits per call. Failed calls are not charged.

days.description: Look back this many days by event date. Default 90, up to 365.

detail.description: Include the full detail of each signal. Default false, which keeps a long list readable.

include_withheld.description: Internal accounts only. Also return signals normally held back as likely misattributed.

limit.description: Companies per page, up to 100. Default 25.

min_weight.description: Floor on how much a signal has to matter, 1-10. Signals we do not weight never clear it.

signal_keys.description: Only these signal types. Values come from get_signal_taxonomy; an unknown key is rejected.

signals_per_company.description: Most signals per company, newest first, up to 100. Default 20.

since.description: Start from this event date, YYYY-MM-DD. Takes priority over days and since_last_pull.

since_last_pull.description: Only what was recorded since the last complete, unfiltered pull. Default false.

watchlist.description: The list, by its id (wl_...) or its exact name.

name: get_watchlist_signals
title: Get Watchlist Signals
